phenomena.claim: Superconductivity: below a material-specific critical temperature, electrical resistance vanishes (Onnes 1911, mercury at 4.2 K) and magnetic flux is actively expelled regardless of field-cooling history (Meissner-Ochsenfeld 1933) -- a macroscopic quantum phase with properties possessed by no constituent electron
phenomena.source: Meissner & Ochsenfeld, 'Ein neuer Effekt bei Eintritt der Supraleitfaehigkeit', Naturwissenschaften 21, 787-788 (1933) -- record verified via bookseller/EJP-reprint listings 2026-09-23; Onnes 1911 (Comm. Phys. Lab. Univ. Leiden; primary not fetched) via the historical account van Delft & Kes, 'The discovery of superconductivity', Physics Today 63(9), 38 (2010) -- record verified via Leiden/OSTI listings 2026-09-23
phenomena.caveat: discovery record is conventional (phonon-mediated) superconductivity; the underived high-Tc case is carried in known_disconnects/open_problems

phenomena.claim: Integer quantum Hall effect: the Hall resistance of a two-dimensional electron gas takes fixed values depending only on fundamental constants, insensitive to the geometry of the device
phenomena.source: v. Klitzing, Dorda & Pepper, 'New Method for High-Accuracy Determination of the Fine-Structure Constant Based on Quantized Hall Resistance', Phys. Rev. Lett. 45, 494 (1980) -- abstract fetched from APS 2026-09-23 ('fixed values which depend only on the fine-structure constant and speed of light, and is insensitive to the geometry of the device')
phenomena.caveat: an emergent quantity exact to metrological precision in a dirty, material-dependent system -- the exactness grading lives in constants/observables

phenomena.claim: Fractional quantum Hall effect: a quantized Hall plateau at rho_xy = 3h/e^2 with a rho_xx minimum at Landau-level filling 1/3 -- a correlated electron liquid with no single-particle explanation
phenomena.source: Tsui, Stormer & Gossard, 'Two-Dimensional Magnetotransport in the Extreme Quantum Limit', Phys. Rev. Lett. 48, 1559 (1982) -- abstract fetched from APS 2026-09-23
phenomena.caveat: the discovery paper's own proposed explanation (Wigner solid / CDW) was superseded by Laughlin's incompressible-fluid account (derived_objects)

phenomena.claim: Fractionally charged quasiparticles are directly observed: shot-noise measurements in the nu = 1/3 regime determine the carrier charge to be e* = e/3, by two independent groups in the same year
phenomena.source: de-Picciotto, Reznikov, Heiblum, Umansky, Bunin & Mahalu, 'Direct Observation of a Fractional Charge', Nature 389, 162-164 (1997), arXiv:cond-mat/9707289; Saminadayar, Glattli, Jin & Etienne, 'Observation of the e/3 Fractionally Charged Laughlin Quasiparticles', Phys. Rev. Lett. 79, 2526 (1997), arXiv:cond-mat/9706307 -- both arXiv abstracts fetched 2026-09-23
phenomena.caveat: the observed carriers are collective excitations: no fractionally charged constituent exists in the substrate (electrons + nuclei carry integer e)

phenomena.claim: Anyonic (fractional exchange) statistics are observed: current cross-correlations of colliding nu = 1/3 quasiparticles yield an exchange phase phi = pi/3, and Fabry-Perot interferometry shows Aharonov-Bohm interference punctuated by discrete anyonic phase slips -- two independent methods in 2020
phenomena.source: Bartolomei et al., 'Fractional statistics in anyon collisions', Science 368, 173-177 (2020), arXiv:2006.13157; Nakamura, Liang, Gardner & Manfra, 'Direct observation of anyonic braiding statistics at the nu=1/3 fractional quantum Hall state', Nature Physics 16, 931 (2020), doi:10.1038/s41567-020-1019-1, arXiv:2006.14115 -- both arXiv abstracts fetched 2026-09-23
phenomena.caveat: a particle statistics realized only as an emergent, effective-level property: the substrate contains fermions only

phenomena.claim: Universality of critical behavior is observed at high precision: the specific-heat exponent of the He-4 superfluid transition is measured in microgravity as alpha = -0.0127 +/- 0.0003 with amplitude ratio A+/A- = 1.053 +/- 0.002, resolution reaching 2 nK from T_lambda with no observed rounding
phenomena.source: Lipa, Nissen, Stricker, Swanson & Chui, 'Specific heat of liquid helium in zero gravity very near the lambda point', Phys. Rev. B 68, 174518 (2003) -- abstract fetched from APS 2026-09-23
phenomena.caveat: sharpest single exponent measurement on record; the cross-material statement (fluids, magnets, alloys sharing exponents by symmetry/dimension class alone) is textbook-standard and carried by the RG formalism entry; universality holds only in the scaling limit near criticality, with measurable corrections to scaling

formalism.claim: Landau paradigm: conventional phases are classified by order parameters acquiring expectation values under spontaneous symmetry breaking (Ginzburg-Landau free-energy functionals); for conventional superconductivity the microscopic completion is BCS theory -- pairing from phonon-mediated attraction yielding gap, condensation energy, and thermodynamics
formalism.source: Bardeen, Cooper & Schrieffer, 'Theory of Superconductivity', Phys. Rev. 108, 1175 (1957) -- abstract fetched from APS 2026-09-23; Ginzburg-Landau 1950 and the Landau order-parameter framework textbook-standard
formalism.caveat: the symmetry-breaking classification is not exhaustive -- topological order falls outside it (symmetries)

formalism.claim: Renormalization-group universality: critical exponents are properties of RG fixed points, shared across microscopically unrelated systems in the same dimension/symmetry class; the Widom-Kadanoff scaling laws follow from the RG flow equations
formalism.source: Wilson, 'Renormalization Group and Critical Phenomena. I. Renormalization Group and the Kadanoff Scaling Picture', Phys. Rev. B 4, 3174 (1971), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.4.3174 -- abstract verified via APS listing 2026-09-23; companion paper PRB 4, 3184 (1971) record listed same day
formalism.caveat: same Wilsonian machinery as quantum_field_theory_eft/formalism (fixed points and universality organize the flow) -- cross-reference, not duplication; condensed matter supplies the experimental leg (phenomena: He-4 lambda point)

formalism.claim: Topological classification of quantized transport: the Hall conductance of a gapped 2D system is a topological invariant (TKNN/Chern integer computed from the Kubo formula), and Laughlin's gauge argument ties the quantization to gauge invariance plus a mobility gap, independent of microscopic detail
formalism.source: Thouless, Kohmoto, Nightingale & den Nijs, 'Quantized Hall Conductance in a Two-Dimensional Periodic Potential', Phys. Rev. Lett. 49, 405 (1982) -- abstract fetched from APS 2026-09-23; Laughlin, 'Quantized Hall conductivity in two dimensions', Phys. Rev. B 23, 5632(R) (1981) -- abstract fetched from APS 2026-09-23
formalism.caveat: the derivation runs through the Kubo linear-response formula -- the response-function pedigree the core's response/memory items draw on is carried in statistical_mechanics_thermodynamics (fluctuation-dissipation entry); cross-reference

primitives.claim: The microscopic substrate of the entire domain is known and uncontested: nonrelativistic electrons and nuclei with Coulomb interactions (plus hbar, m, e) -- the 'Theory of Everything' Hamiltonian of Laughlin-Pines; what is at issue in this domain is never the substrate but deducibility of the emergent level from it
primitives.source: Laughlin & Pines, 'The Theory of Everything', Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 97(1), 28-31 (2000) -- record verified via ADS/PNAS listings 2026-09-23 (direct solution accurate only up to ~10 particles)
primitives.caveat: this makes condensed matter the clean laboratory for emergence claims: unlike quantum-gravity settings, both levels are independently accessible

primitives.claim: Emergent structures of the domain -- order parameters, quasiparticles, effective gauge fields, topological invariants -- are not primitives: each is defined only at the collective/effective level and has no referent for a single constituent
primitives.source: textbook-standard (Landau quasiparticle and order-parameter concepts; Anderson 1972 in symmetries for the emergence statement)
primitives.caveat: bears on the core's emergence existence-proofs and recurrence (7) 'effective-level pinning with substrate freedom' (RRP_00_REQUIREMENTS_PICTURE_01 SS4): recorded here as what exists, no requirement asserted

derived_objects.claim: Conventional superconductivity is derived from the microscopic level: BCS obtain the paired ground state, energy gap, second-order transition, specific heat, penetration depth, and the isotope effect from phonon-mediated electron attraction -- the flagship demonstrated emergence-by-derivation in the corpus
derived_objects.source: Bardeen, Cooper & Schrieffer, Phys. Rev. 108, 1175 (1957) -- abstract fetched from APS 2026-09-23
derived_objects.caveat: existence proof that a qualitatively new macroscopic phase can be strictly deduced from a known substrate; scope is conventional superconductors -- the high-Tc case resists the same treatment (known_disconnects)

derived_objects.claim: Fractionally charged excitations were derived before observation: Laughlin's variational ground state describes condensation of the 2D electron gas into an incompressible quantum fluid whose excitations carry fractional charge -- confirmed 14 years later by shot noise (phenomena)
derived_objects.source: Laughlin, 'Anomalous Quantum Hall Effect: An Incompressible Quantum Fluid with Fractionally Charged Excitations', Phys. Rev. Lett. 50, 1395 (1983) -- abstract fetched from APS 2026-09-23
derived_objects.caveat: prediction-before-measurement grade for an emergent quantum number

derived_objects.claim: Quantization of Hall conductance is theorem-grade for interacting systems: for 2D lattice fermions with finite-range interactions and a gapped ground state, the Hall conductance is quantized in integer multiples of e^2/h without averaging assumptions, with corrections decaying stretched-exponentially in system size
derived_objects.source: Hastings & Michalakis, 'Quantization of Hall Conductance For Interacting Electrons Without Averaging Assumptions', arXiv:0911.4706 [math-ph] -- abstract fetched 2026-09-23
derived_objects.caveat: the rigorous instance of topological protection as the mechanism of emergent exactness: the exact value survives interactions and disorder because it is an invariant of the gapped phase, not a fine-tuned property of the substrate -- the mechanism behind the core's recurrence (7) pattern; hypotheses are gap + finite range, and the fractional case is not covered by this theorem

derived_objects.claim: Emergent gauge fields are standard derived objects: deconfined lattice gauge structures (with matter partons) arise as the effective low-energy description of frustrated quantum spin models -- structures that are effective without being fundamental, in systems whose substrate demonstrably contains no gauge field
derived_objects.source: Savary & Balents, 'Quantum Spin Liquids', Rep. Prog. Phys. 80, 016502 (2017), arXiv:1601.03742 -- abstract fetched 2026-09-23 (gauge theories and partons as the theoretical framework); Wen, 'Zoo of quantum-topological phases of matter', Rev. Mod. Phys. 89, 041004 (2017), arXiv:1610.03911 -- abstract fetched 2026-09-23
derived_objects.caveat: review-level and abstract-verified: theoretical existence is community-standard, while material realization is still contested (open_problems); bears on core item C(ii) -- emergent-substrate schemes must name their Weinberg-Witten exit, and these models name it (no Lorentz invariance; see known_disconnects) -- and on the core's emergence existence-proofs; no requirement asserted

empirical_inputs.claim: Effective theories of the domain take material-specific inputs: band structures, effective masses, Landau parameters, pairing strengths, T_c values, and gap magnitudes are measured or fit, not derived within the effective theory; ab initio computation from the substrate Hamiltonian succeeds only partially (density-functional methods for weakly correlated materials)
empirical_inputs.caveat: the contrast entry: topologically protected quantities (constants) need none of these inputs -- that split, exact-by-topology vs input-laden, is the domain's own version of effective-level pinning

constants.claim: von Klitzing constant R_K = h/e^2 = 25 812.807 45... ohm, exact: fixed by the 2019 SI redefinition (exact h and e); the quantum Hall effect realizes the ohm metrologically
constants.source: CODATA 2022 recommended values, NIST CUU (physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/cuu/Value?rk) -- page fetched 2026-09-23; standard uncertainty stated 'exact'
constants.caveat: exact by definition since 2019; the empirical content is the pre-2019 measurement chain plus the material-independence tests recorded in observables -- an emergent collective quantity serving as a fundamental-constant standard

symmetries.claim: Spontaneous symmetry breaking organizes the conventional phase inventory (crystals, magnets, superfluids, superconductors), and Anderson's 'More is Different' states the domain's emergence reading: at each level of complexity broken symmetry produces genuinely new laws, properties, and concepts -- 'the whole becomes not only more than but very different from the sum of its parts'
symmetries.source: Anderson, 'More Is Different', Science 177(4047), 393-396 (1972), doi:10.1126/science.177.4047.393 -- record verified via Semantic Scholar DOI lookup 2026-09-23 (science.org direct fetch 403); broken-symmetry classification textbook-standard
symmetries.caveat: Anderson's constructionist-vs-reductionist thesis is an interpretive claim by a primary architect of the field, recorded as the community's emergence charter, not as an adjudicated result

symmetries.claim: Topological order falls outside the Landau symmetry-breaking classification: gapped phases exist with no local order parameter, distinguished instead by patterns of long-range entanglement and topological invariants (ground-state degeneracy, edge structure, anyon content)
symmetries.source: Wen, 'Zoo of quantum-topological phases of matter', Rev. Mod. Phys. 89, 041004 (2017), arXiv:1610.03911 -- abstract fetched 2026-09-23
symmetries.caveat: the classification concept is community-standard; the complete classification program is open (open_problems)

limits.claim: Landau Fermi-liquid theory is recovered as the generic RG fixed point of interacting fermions in d > 1 with a rotationally invariant Fermi surface: modes near the Fermi surface flow to the Fermi-liquid fixed point, with superconducting pairing as the identified relevant instability (and Luttinger liquids in d = 1)
limits.source: Shankar, 'Renormalization Group Approach to Interacting Fermions', Rev. Mod. Phys. 66, 129 (1994), arXiv:cond-mat/9307009 -- abstract fetched 2026-09-23
limits.caveat: edge type LIMIT_RELATION; explains why a weakly-interacting quasiparticle description emerges from a strongly-interacting substrate -- effective-level structure stable against microscopic detail

limits.claim: Ginzburg-Landau theory is recovered from BCS microscopics near T_c (Gor'kov): the phenomenological order-parameter functional is the controlled limit of the microscopic theory, fixing its coefficients
limits.source: converter: fetch of the bibliographic record Gor'kov, Sov. Phys. JETP 9, 1364 (1959) ('Microscopic derivation of the Ginzburg-Landau equations in the theory of superconductivity'), or a standard-text statement of the derivation (e.g. de Gennes; Tinkham ch. 4)
limits.caveat: textbook-standard content; recorded TO-VERIFY until a checked record is attached; edge type LIMIT_RELATION

known_connections.claim: The Anderson-Higgs mechanism is a condensed-matter export to fundamental physics: gauge-boson mass generation without explicit symmetry breaking was exhibited first in the superconducting plasma (Yang-Mills bosons 'need not be massless'), then transferred to the electroweak sector
known_connections.source: Anderson, 'Plasmons, Gauge Invariance, and Mass', Phys. Rev. 130, 439 (1963) -- abstract fetched from APS 2026-09-23; electroweak side carried by gauge_theory / quantum_field_theory_eft -- cross-reference
known_connections.caveat: pedigree edge: an effective-level condensed-matter structure supplied the mechanism later found in the substrate-level Standard Model; typing to the seven-class scheme is Stage-3 work

known_connections.claim: This domain supplies the laboratory instances of the adjudicated core's recurrence (7), 'effective-level pinning with substrate freedom': the same exact effective quantity (quantized Hall resistance) is realized on distinct substrates (GaAs heterostructures, epitaxial graphene) with no measured difference, while substrate-level properties vary freely
known_connections.source: archive: RRP_00_REQUIREMENTS_PICTURE_01.md SS4 recurrence (7) and SS2 item B (effective-sector pinning); physics legs = the OBSERVED entries of this record plus observables (Janssen et al. universality test)
known_connections.caveat: scope: the mapping of condensed-matter instances onto the core pattern is in-house, unreviewed adjudication and can never upgrade by repetition; the physics legs stand independently as OBSERVED/COMMUNITY-DERIVED entries; nothing here asserts the pattern is required of any theory

known_disconnects.claim: Knowing the substrate does NOT in practice yield the emergent level: the 'Theory of Everything' Hamiltonian is exactly known for every material, yet direct solution fails beyond ~10 particles and emergent phenomena (superconductivity, FQHE fractions) were found by experiment plus effective-level reasoning, not deduced bottom-up
known_disconnects.source: Laughlin & Pines, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 97(1), 28-31 (2000) -- record verified via ADS/PNAS listings 2026-09-23
known_disconnects.caveat: a deducibility-in-practice statement, not an in-principle underivability theorem; BCS (derived_objects) shows the derivation can succeed post hoc for specific phenomena

known_disconnects.claim: Weinberg-Witten-type constraints do NOT bind condensed-matter emergent gauge/graviton analogues: the theorem's Lorentz-invariance and covariant-stress-tensor hypotheses fail by construction in nonrelativistic lattice systems, so emergent gauge structure there is a named-exit case, not a counterexample
known_disconnects.source: theorem scope carried by quantum_field_theory_eft/known_disconnects (Weinberg-Witten entry) -- cross-reference, not restated; the lattice systems' lack of Lorentz invariance is textbook-standard
known_disconnects.caveat: bears on core item C(ii): emergent substrata must name their theorem exit -- condensed-matter models name it (no Lorentz invariance), which is exactly why they are existence proofs for emergent gauge structure but not for relativistic emergent gravitons; no requirement asserted

open_problems.claim: No first-principles derivation of high-temperature (cuprate) superconductivity exists: four decades after discovery (Bednorz-Mueller 1986), the mechanism, phase-diagram complexity, and T_c values remain underived from the microscopic Hamiltonian
open_problems.source: Keimer, Kivelson, Norman, Uchida & Zaanen, 'High Temperature Superconductivity in the Cuprates', Nature 518, 179 (2015), arXiv:1409.4673 -- abstract fetched 2026-09-23 (open questions on the normal state and collective fluctuations; theory drawing on string-theoretic and quantum-information methods, i.e. unresolved); discovery record: Bednorz & Mueller, Z. Phys. B 64, 189-193 (1986) -- record verified via Wikidata/publisher listings 2026-09-23
open_problems.caveat: the domain's standing counterweight to its own emergence-by-derivation successes: demonstrated emergence does not imply demonstrated deducibility

open_problems.claim: No material is established at consensus level as a quantum spin liquid with deconfined emergent gauge excitations: candidate materials exist, but experimental identification remains unsettled
open_problems.source: converter: full-text check of the experimental-status sections of Savary & Balents, Rep. Prog. Phys. 80, 016502 (2017), or a newer status review of spin-liquid candidates
open_problems.caveat: widely held community assessment; recorded TO-VERIFY until the review's own status language is extracted; the FQHE side of emergent-structure observation is not affected (anyons are observed -- phenomena)

observables.claim: The material-independence of quantized Hall resistance is tested directly: graphene vs GaAs/AlGaAs comparison finds no difference within a relative standard uncertainty of 8.6e-11 -- the most stringent universality-of-quantization test on record; alongside it the domain's precision observables include critical exponents (alpha_He4 = -0.0127(3)), gap spectra, and transport coefficients
observables.source: Janssen, Fletcher, Goebel, Williams, Tzalenchuk, Yakimova, Kubatkin, Lara-Avila & Falko, 'Graphene, universality of the quantum Hall effect and redefinition of the SI system', New J. Phys. 13, 093026 (2011), arXiv:1105.4055 -- abstract fetched 2026-09-23 ('no difference of the quantized resistance value within ... 8.6e-11')
observables.caveat: two chemically and structurally unrelated substrates realizing one exact effective number -- the direct data leg of the known_connections core-pattern entry

alternative_formulations.claim: The fractional quantum Hall liquid admits coexisting effective descriptions -- Laughlin trial wavefunctions, composite-fermion mapping (Jain), Chern-Simons effective field theory, and chiral edge theories -- agreeing on the observed fractions and quasiparticle content
alternative_formulations.source: converter: abstract fetches of Jain, Phys. Rev. Lett. 63, 199 (1989) (composite fermions) and Zhang, Hansson & Kivelson, Phys. Rev. Lett. 62, 82 (1989) (effective-field-theory model for the FQHE); Laughlin 1983 already verified (derived_objects)
alternative_formulations.caveat: one emergent phase, several inequivalent-looking effective theories with matching observables -- recorded TO-VERIFY until the two named records are checked

domain_of_validity.claim: Topological exactness holds only within the gapped, localized regime: quantized Hall transport requires a mobility gap, low temperature, and sub-breakdown currents (thermal activation and high-current breakdown degrade it, as bounded in Laughlin's original error estimate); universality of critical exponents holds only asymptotically near criticality with measurable corrections to scaling
domain_of_validity.source: Laughlin, Phys. Rev. B 23, 5632(R) (1981) -- abstract fetched from APS 2026-09-23 (error estimate from thermal activation to the mobility edge); QHE breakdown and corrections-to-scaling phenomenology textbook-standard
domain_of_validity.caveat: emergent exactness is conditional exactness: exact within the protected phase, with sharply stated conditions -- not exact simpliciter
